proposals.narrative: The Lyra GmbH invoice INV-LG-2291 for EUR 8,000 was settled by wire on 2026-08-14 for USD 8,712.00. Converting EUR 8,000 at 1.0890 gives USD 8,712.00, which agrees exactly with the bank line, so accounts payable is relieved in full with no FX variance.

Repair after VERITY-FX-003. Policy requires the transaction-date spot rate from an approved provider. The invoice transaction date is 2026-08-11 and the approved APEX-REF-RATES spot rate for that date is 1.0785, giving a carrying value of USD 8,628.00. The bank settled USD 8,712.00, so the USD 84.00 difference is a realized FX loss rather than a reduction of payables.

controllerDecisions.rationale: Rate is from an approved provider but dated the settlement day. Policy requires the transaction-date spot rate. Relieving AP at 5,400.00 also hides the FX loss.

Approved provider and spot rate, but dated the settlement day rather than the invoice transaction date of 2026-08-27. Same problem as the Meridian Cloud item, and it hides the USD 46.00 realized FX loss.
Transaction-date spot rate from the approved provider, FX loss recognized correctly.

controlPRs.failureMode: Settlement-date FX rate used in place of the transaction-date spot rate
controlPRs.specAmendment: Pack v1 checks that an FX observation comes from an approved provider and is a spot rate, but not that its rate date matches the invoice transaction date. Two controller rejections in the v1 baseline used approved spot rates dated the settlement day, so both passed controls and reached review, and each relieved payables at an amount that concealed a realized FX loss. Add a control requiring fx.rateDate to equal the transaction date on the cited supporting document.

onFail.title: FX rate date matches the transaction date
onFail.requiredRepair: Retrieve the approved spot rate observed on the invoice transaction date, recalculate the entry, recognize any settlement difference as realized FX gain or loss, and cite the exact observation.
